answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, with transition mass attenuated at each step and normalized by node credibility. A sybil cluster forms a sparse external cut: its low conductance limits inflow from honest nodes, while min-cut transitivity bounds its stationary mass and therefore aggregate voting weight. Even a jetty, summit, or ridge of colluding identities cannot bypass this bottleneck.
